newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins slip on fear of more US rate hikes.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins slip on fear of more US rate hikes.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds eased on Wednesday, tracking the decline of emerging markets on fears of another U.S. interest rate hike after today's statistics on durable goods, dealers said.
The U.S. Commerce Department said on Wednesday that durable goods orders rose 1.5 percent in February compared to an upwardly revised 4.1 percent increase in January.
The data brought many market analysts to believe that yet another short-term interest rate rise could come in May.

"As before, there is no problem about Russia. It is just a big worry about U.S. interest rates," Eurobank dealer Olivier Coursault said. "The market got more depressed by today's (U.S.) data on durables."
Dealers said prices had been slipping since morning, stopping only briefly when the Russian government got yet another batch of liberal reformers on board on Wednesday.
"Foreigners like clarity in such matters, but U.S. traders have stepped in and are still pushing prices down further," a Russian bank said.
Former Economy Minister Yevgeny Yasin has been named a minister without portfolio in the new Russian government, Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin told a news conference on Wednesday.
Chernomyrdin also said that Alexei Kudrin, an ally of new First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais was appointed First Deputy Finance Minister.
Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Kulikov would retain day-to-day charge of Russia's tax and customs services.

But foreign trade activities and policy-making in the tax and customs services would be the responsibility of Alfred Kokh, another deputy prime minister who deals with privatisation and who is close to Chubais.
